solution.title: Apply the Power Rule
solution.explanation: The power rule states that the derivative of \(x^n\) is \(nx^{n-1}\). We apply this to each term in the polynomial.

solution.title: Differentiate Each Term
solution.explanation:
For the first term, \(3x^2\), the derivative is \(3 \cdot 2x^{2-1} = 6x\).
For the second term, \(2x\), the derivative is \(2 \cdot 1x^{1-1} = 2\).
The derivative of a constant, -5, is 0.

solution.title: Combine the Results
solution.explanation: Summing the derivatives of each term gives us the final answer: \(f'(x) = 6x + 2\).

title: Solve the linear equation 2x + 3 = 11
problem: Find the value of x that satisfies the equation \(2x + 3 = 11\).

solution.title: Isolate the variable term
solution.explanation: To get the term with x by itself, subtract 3 from both sides of the equation: \(2x + 3 - 3 = 11 - 3\), which simplifies to \(2x = 8\).

solution.title: Solve for x
solution.explanation: Now, divide both sides by 2 to solve for x: \(2x / 2 = 8 / 2\), which gives \(x = 4\).
